R-ops-1 (Switch to Paylane has no way back once the Stripe account is closed) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The Stripe client is deleted and replaced by the Paylane client in the same
release. There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain. The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep a way back for the provider switch-over: keep the Stripe client behind a configuration switch (or a percentage rollout) selecting the provider, and keep the Stripe account open until Paylane has run in production for at least one full deploy cycle (about a week) with settlement confirmed. Failure scenario: Paylane rejects or times out on authorizations, or a defect in the new client shows up, two days after the release — deploying the previous version calls Stripe, whose account is already closed, so card payments stay down until a fix is written and shipped in a new release. Also state in the design how operators detect a Paylane failure rate rising after the switch.
findings.title: Switch to Paylane has no way back once the Stripe account is closed

findings.evidence:
A new worker, `settlement-worker`, runs at 02:00, fetches the day's Paylane
payments and matches them to orders. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Decide in the design how the worker is observed: a structured log at start and end of each run (run date, payments fetched, matched, unmatched), a metric or last-success timestamp, and an alert when the 02:00 run fails or does not complete (CronJob failed job, missed schedule, or Paylane API unreachable). Failure scenario: the Paylane API is unreachable at 02:00 or the job crashes — the CronJob fails, nothing is written, and since the only alert in the spec fires for a payment without order, finance sees no alert and the day's payments stay unsettled silently. Say also whether a failed night is re-run (catching up a missed day) and that a re-run is safe to repeat.
findings.title: settlement-worker has no failure signal, so a missed nightly run goes unnoticed
